en.label: English
en.title: AFRUZA SENT ME SOME DATES
stanzas: Afruza sent some dates for me
Afruza sent me some dates from Mecca.
Taking the black dates in my hands
No thought of Allah or God crossed my mind
The picture of the date plants
Is flashing on my mental screen
The picture of the date plants
Standing bathed in the misty moonlight
Is flashing on my mental screen
Those that do not call out for Allah and God
They call out for human beings
Who even after having a Mosque
Had built a temple in her bosom.
Afruza sent some dates for me

hi.label: हिन्दी
hi.title: अफ़रूज़ा ने मुझे कुछ खजूर भेजे
stanzas: अफ़रूज़ा ने मेरे लिए कुछ खजूर भेजे,
एक पैकेट में जिस पर भाईचारा लिखा था।
अफ़रूज़ा ने मुझे कुछ खजूर भेजे,
एक पैकेट में जिस पर भाईचारा लिखा था।
किसी ने मेरे कान में फुसफुसाया:
अफ़रूज़ा ने मुझे मक्का से कुछ खजूर भेजे।
काले खजूर हाथों में लेते हुए
मेरे मन में अल्लाह या ईश्वर का कोई ख़याल नहीं आया।
मेरे मन के परदे पर चमक रहा है।
मेरे मन के परदे पर चमक रहा है।
जो अल्लाह और ईश्वर को नहीं पुकारते,
अपने हृदय में मंदिर बनाया था।
अफ़रूज़ा ने मेरे लिए कुछ खजूर भेजे,
एक पैकेट में जिस पर भाईचारा लिखा था।

en.label: English
en.title: The Temple of Afruza Akhtar
stanzas: Even after having a mosque in the bosom
Afruza Akhtar was not at peace
Till she had a temple in her bosom.
But one thing is true that Afruza asked me-
Wherefrom `d the bricks be brought to build the temple?
It needn`t be brought from Ayodhya or Vrindavan
Just fetch from the nearby kiln
Get Cement and sand from the petty shopkeeper
Near your hour house, the poorest one
The one who remained with the smallest shop because he couldn`t lie
And you need not fetch water from the river
Countless corpses floated down the river
How troubled the river was being forced to carry down those dead bodies
The rivers do not remain river any more Afruza
So to mix the mortar get water from the well
After the temple was made in the bosom of Afruza
How excited she was to tell me
Now Allah and Bhagwan relishes food
From the same plate in her bosom
Shares the same bed to sleep
How are they to look at?
So now it has become rather difficult for her

en.label: English
en.title: Two Poems
stanzas: Let us go to eat out today
A white cool wind is blowing
Let us go to eat out today
Let those two old hands of ours
Let us go to eat out today
chat at the dining table today
and let us watch them closely
The shadows can’t tell a hie
as they have no tongue to speak
Let us listen to them today
A chilly white wind is blowing
Let us go to dine out today
one feels like taking entire world
and dangerous curves of this world
